title: Open unit forces etale projections in a flat groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t:R\to U$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. If the unit $e:U\to R$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], both $s$ and $t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No Noetherian, reducedness, field or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04R9 (lemma-sheaf-differentials), together with morphisms.tex Tags 02G5 (lemma-unramified-omega-zero) and 02GV (lemma-flat-unramified-etale); applied in the final paragraph of stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06N0.

proof.text: Put $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ and $Q=R\times_{t,U,t}R$. Define $\phi:P\to Q$ by $(a,b)\mapsto(i(a),b)$. This is a scheme map by the fibre-product universal property since $t(i(a))=s(a)=t(b)$. Its inverse $Q\to P$ is given by the same formula, since $s(i(a))=t(a)=t(b)$. The two composites are the identities because inversion in a groupoid satisfies $i^2=1$. Thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04R9 (lemma-sheaf-differentials), proof diagram, with inversion on the first factor instead of the second.

proof.text: Define $j:R\to P$ by $j(a)=(i(a),a)$; this lands in $P$ since $s(i(a))=t(a)$. The square with top $j$, left $s:R\to U$, right $c:P\to R$, and bottom $e:U\to R$ commutes, since $c(i(a),a)=e(s(a))$, and it is cartesian. For maps $a,b:T\to R$ and $u:T\to U$ with $s(a)=t(b)$ and $c(a,b)=e(u)$, applying $s$ and $t$ gives $s(b)=sc(a,b)=se(u)=u$ and $t(a)=tc(a,b)=te(u)=u$. By associativity and the unit and inverse axioms, $b=c(e(s(a)),b)=c(c(i(a),a),b)=c(i(a),c(a,b))=c(i(a),e(u))=i(a)$, the last equality because $s(i(a))=t(a)=u$. Hence $a=i(b)$, so $(a,b)=j(b)$ and $u=s(b)$: the map $b:T\to R$ is a lift, and it is the only one because the second projection of $j$ is the identity of $R$. This verifies the universal property on arbitrary test schemes, not only points.

source.place: Tag 04R9 (lemma-sheaf-differentials), cartesian square in the proof, with the two factors inverted/swapped in the displayed parametrization.

proof.text: Since $e$ is an open immersion, the projection $U\times_{e,R,c}P\to P$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. By step 2 and the uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $j$ is this projection composed with an isomorphism $R\cong U\times_{e,R,c}P$ of its source, so $j$ is an open immersion. Under the isomorphism $\phi$ of step 1, $\phi j(a)=(i(i(a)),a)=(a,a)$, hence $\phi j=\Delta_t:R\to Q$. The definition of open immersion is invariant under composing with isomorphisms of source and target: the image open subset and the structure-sheaf isomorphism are carried across them. Therefore $\Delta_t$ is an open immersion.

The involution $i:R\to R$ exchanges $s$ and $t$. Thus $I:R\times_{s,U,s}R\to R\times_{t,U,t}R$, $(a,b)\mapsto(i(a),i(b))$, is an isomorphism with inverse the same formula, and $I\Delta_s=\Delta_t i$. Consequently $\Delta_s=I^{-1}\Delta_t i$ is also an open immersion, by the same invariance of the defining homeomorphism and sheaf isomorphism under isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04R9 (lemma-sheaf-differentials), symmetric use with source and target exchanged.

proof.text: Each projection is locally of finite type: apply [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] with base $U$, source $R$ with structure map $s$ (resp. $t$), which is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, target $U$ with structure map $\mathrm{id}_U$, and $h=s$ (resp. $t$). The identity is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], since every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $U$ is covered by itself and $A$ is generated by $1$ over $A$. The lemma gives that $s$ and $t$ are locally of finite type. Together with the open diagonals in steps 3 and 4, this is unramifiedness by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Finally, each projection is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] by hypothesis; these properties and unramifiedness are precisely the three clauses of [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Both projections are therefore etale.
